before: Concurrent tracked splits of one paragraph each wrote their proposed paragraph mark on the paragraph they split, so the merged paragraph showed one proposal, the other new paragraph mark showed none, and Reject All left a split. Two splits by each of two peers, a break at a paragraph's end beside a split, and siblings an undo or redo listed again could show out of text order with an empty paragraph.
after: Each proposed paragraph mark a concurrent split wrote shows on the paragraph shown right before that split's new paragraph: the materializer shows it there and the projection of a local edit lists it there before the edit addresses either paragraph. Paragraphs of a run of concurrent splits, each peer's later splits of its own new paragraphs included, order by where each one's own last split fell when those characters all stand in one live text, and otherwise by their split of the paragraph the run follows, a break at a paragraph's end records a split at that end, and a sibling an undo or redo lists again right before its own removed entry in a run belongs to the run; a paragraph listed there anew, whose record its first entry brought, shows where its author put it. A redo that puts back a moved copy, as a redo of a split does, marks it as a moved copy again besides the restore mark, so it shows by document order among the moved copies of its characters and does not hide behind a copy a peer split off at the same time. Split points are written only by the edit that creates the paragraph. Reject All restores the paragraph. The tests cover two peers with up to three typed breaks or Paragraph.split calls each, a single call with two split points, three peers with one split each, one peer undoing and redoing online, and both peers undoing and then redoing offline: every piece shows in text order.
reason: Where a proposal shows and which paragraphs a run holds are rules over the same shared state, so they belong to repairVersion 3, which these records already introduce; replicas with repairVersion 2 refuse these rooms. The projection moves a proposal with ordinary child splices, as merged property copies and adoption already do. A redo of a moved copy writes one more text mark, of a kind every replica of this format already reads; no field changes.
